parakeet: If an entity cannot be observed, measured, tested, falsified, or independently verified, then we completely lose the diagnostic ability to tell the difference between hidden and imaginary. In the physical sciences, there is a fundamental operational rule. If a thing is truly invisible, immeasurable, and leaves absolutely no physical footprint, it produces precisely zero observable effects on the universe. And if it produces zero observable effects, it's functionally and scientifically identical to non-existence. We can't see dark matter. This is a massive false equivalency, and it's time to shut it down completely. But we don't accept their existence because a book told us to have faith in them. We accept them because their effects are consistently detectable, mathematically predictive, and independently verifiable. Anyone anywhere in the world, regardless of their culture, language, or personal beliefs, can drop a rock and measure gravity. They can build a particle accelerator and track an electron. They can observe the exact same effects and arrive at the exact same conclusions. The deeper, inescapable issue is that God's existence is debated in a way that gravity, planets, and chemistry simply are not. There are zero competing global factions killing each other over the true nature of photosynthesis. There are no apologetic ministries dedicated to defending the existence of the moon. Science handles the unseen through evidence and universal consensus. Theology handles the unseen through excuses and perpetual division. At the end of the day, we have to make a choice about how we determine what is real. We can have a single honest standard of evidence, one that applies to gravity, biology, history, and every claim ever made about our world. But if you have to lower your standards of truth to find God, you aren't discovering reality. You're protecting an illusion. If a creator exists, it should be the most undeniable, self-evident anchor of human knowledge. It shouldn't require a lifetime of intellectual acrobatics, a library of apologetics, and a stack of unverified doctrines just to make it indistinguishable from non-existence. For centuries, skeptics have been handed the burden of proof. We've been asked, how do you explain the universe without God? But that question is a distraction. The real question, the one Christianity simply cannot escape, is why the answer to everything is completely missing from anything we can actually verify. If we cannot detect it, measure it, predict it, or distinguish it from imagination, then the word existence has lost its meaning. Theology has already done that for us by defining him into total obscurity.
